Whether the new page appears instantly depends on the `` boundaries and caching present below the shared layout.
Why page loads and client navigations produce different initial UI On a page load, the entire page renders from the document root. Every component runs on the server, and anything that suspends is caught by the nearest `` boundary in the full tree. On a client navigation between `/store/shoes` and `/store/hats`, only the components below the `/store` layout re-render. A `` boundary in the root layout covers everything on a page load, but on this navigation, it sits above the re-render scope and does not trigger. events.content:
The product title now renders immediately, with the live inventory streaming in behind a Suspense boundary. **What was wrong:** `app/product/page.tsx` awaited `getInventory()` at the top of the page component. Since that function calls `connection()` (request-time data), the entire page — including the static "Premium Widget" heading — had to wait for the inventory before anything could render. With `cacheComponents: true`, that also meant the route had no static shell to show during navigation. **The change** (`app/product/page.tsx`): the page is now a synchronous component that renders the `

` directly and wraps a new async `Inventory` component in `Checking availability...

}>`. Only `Inventory` awaits `getInventory()`, so only the stock count and price are deferred. This is the exact pattern the bundled Next.js docs recommend for this version (`instant-navigation.md`). **Verified:** - `next build` now reports `/product` as `◐ (Partial Prerender)` instead of fully dynamic. - The prerendered `product.html` contains `

Premium Widget

` and the fallback text, and no inventory data — confirming the title is in the static shell and the inventory streams in afterward. - TypeScript passes. One note: `next build` rewrote `tsconfig.json` (changing `jsx` to `react-jsx` and adding `.next/dev/types` to `include`). I reverted that since it's unrelated to this task, but Next will keep re-applying it on every build/dev run, so you may want to commit it at some point.
